# Summary

Progressive filtering of the dataset. After each filtering steps different metrics are measured to asses the dataset refinement. These key metrics include broad sence heritability and normality of the data.


# Setup

## Packages

This analysis depends on the following packages:

```{r library}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("tidyverse"))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("lme4"))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("Hmisc"))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("corrplot"))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("emmeans"))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("patchwork"))
```

## Helper functions

Two helper functions are created:\
- `calculate_broad_heritability()` giving the broad sense heritability (H^2^) and the number of genotypes of a given dataset.\
- `create_correlation_plot()` to calculate the correlations between experimental sessions.

```{r}
source("../../broad_heritability_function.R")
source("../../create_correlation_plot.R")
```

# Broad-sense heritability calculations

## Raw dataset

```{r}
#| echo: true

data250_afabae_00 <- read.csv("../../../../../../01.data/2023_screen_specifics_251genotypes/02.aphis_fabae_on_faba_collection/aphis_fabae_fecundity_on_faba_collection_2024-04-02.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, sep = ",") %>%  
  mutate(ivip = as.factor(ivip)) %>% 
  mutate(session = as.factor(session)) 

res <- calculate_broad_heritability(data = data250_afabae_00)
```
we can't use our dataset like this, we need to clean it first.

::: callout-tip
Conclusions:\
- Heritability is equal to `r round(res$heritability, digits=3)`.\
- There are `r res$number_of_genotypes` genotypes in total.\
- There are `r res$number_of_notation` measurements in total.
:::

## Missing data

First step we remove all line with a NA for larvae count. 

```{r}
data250_afabae_01 <- data250_afabae_00 %>% filter(!is.na(larvae_total_number))
data250_afabae_01$ivip <- droplevels(data250_afabae_01$ivip)

res2 <- calculate_broad_heritability(data = data250_afabae_01)
```

::: callout-tip
Conclusions:\
- Heritability is equal to `r round(res2$heritability, digits=3)`.\
- There are `r res2$number_of_genotypes` genotypes in total.\
- There are `r res2$number_of_notation` measurements in total.
:::

```{r}
#| eval: false
create_correlation_plot(data250_afabae_01, 
                         group_cols = c("genotype", "session"), 
                         value_col = "larvae_total_number")
```

## Remove observations with no adult alive

We chose to remove all data from plants on which no adult aphid was found. This decision was made to get rid of larvae installation bias and only assess the reproduction ability of the aphid.

When the adult aphid dies, the number of larvae will drop but only because the adult stayed spent less time on the plant and not because the plant was not suitable for the reproduction.

```{r}
#| echo: true

data250_afabae_02<- data250_afabae_01 %>% filter(adult_alive != "0") #remove if no adult
data250_afabae_02$ivip <- droplevels(data250_afabae_02$ivip)

res3 <- calculate_broad_heritability(data = data250_afabae_02)
```

::: callout-note
Conclusions:\
- Heritability is equal to `r round(res3$heritability, digits=3)`.\
- There are `r res3$number_of_genotypes` genotypes in total.\
- There are `r res3$number_of_notation` measurements in total.
:::

Heritability strongly increases. 602 measurements are lost. The number of genotype stays the same.

```{r}
#| eval: false
create_correlation_plot(data250_afabae_02, 
                         group_cols = c("genotype", "session"), 
                         value_col = "larvae_total_number")
```

```{r normality after adult removal}
#| echo: true
#| fig-width: 8

# With outliers
p_with <- data250_afabae_02 %>% 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(sample=larvae_total_number)) +
  stat_qq() +
  stat_qq_line() +
  labs(y = "Observed quantiles", x = "Theoretical quantiles") +
  ggtitle("With outliers") +
  theme_bw()
p_with
```
We observ few outlier data on both side of the distribution. To remove these data we use the Interquartile range method (IQR). This will help inproving normality of the data. 

## Outliers removal

```{r comparison of qqplots with and without outliers}

x<-1.5
IQR_value <- IQR(data250_afabae_02$larvae_total_number)
lower_bound <- quantile(data250_afabae_02$larvae_total_number, 0.25) - x * IQR_value
upper_bound <- quantile(data250_afabae_02$larvae_total_number, 0.75) + x * IQR_value

# Filter out outliers
data250_afabae_03 <- data250_afabae_02[data250_afabae_02$larvae_total_number >= lower_bound & data250_afabae_02$larvae_total_number <= upper_bound, ]

# Identify the rows that were removed (outliers)
removed_outliers <- data250_afabae_02[data250_afabae_02$larvae_total_number < lower_bound | data250_afabae_02$larvae_total_number > upper_bound, ]

res4 <- calculate_broad_heritability(data = data250_afabae_03)


#| fig-width: 8

# Without outliers
p_without <- data250_afabae_03 %>% 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(sample=larvae_total_number)) +
  stat_qq() +
  stat_qq_line() +
  labs(y = "Observed quantiles", x = "Theoretical quantiles") +
  ggtitle("Without outliers") +
  theme_bw()

p_with + p_without 
```

\newpage

# Final filtering: keep genotypes with at least 4 repetitions

To make sure the data we use for the GWAS are reliable we set a threshold for the minimal number of repetition to keep a genotype.
```{r broad sense heritability 4}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true

data250_afabae_04_4 <- data250_afabae_03 %>%
  group_by(ivip) %>%           # Group by genotype
  filter(n() >= 4) %>%             # Keep only groups with 6 or more repetitions
  ungroup()  
data250_afabae_04_4$ivip <- droplevels(data250_afabae_04_4$ivip)

res5_4 <- calculate_broad_heritability(data = data250_afabae_04_4)
```

```{r broad sense heritability 5}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true

data250_afabae_04_5 <- data250_afabae_03 %>%
  group_by(ivip) %>%           # Group by genotype
  filter(n() >= 5) %>%             # Keep only groups with 6 or more repetitions
  ungroup()  
data250_afabae_04_5$ivip <- droplevels(data250_afabae_04_5$ivip)

res5_5 <- calculate_broad_heritability(data = data250_afabae_04_5)
```


```{r broad sense heritability 6}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true

data250_afabae_04_6 <- data250_afabae_03 %>%
  group_by(ivip) %>%           # Group by genotype
  filter(n() >= 6) %>%             # Keep only groups with 6 or more repetitions
  ungroup()  
data250_afabae_04_6$ivip <- droplevels(data250_afabae_04_6$ivip)

res5_6 <- calculate_broad_heritability(data = data250_afabae_04_6)
```

::: callout-important
Conclusions:\
- Heritability is equal to `r round(res4$heritability, digits=3)`.\
- There are `r res4$number_of_genotypes` genotypes in total.\
- There are `r res4$number_of_notation` measurements in total.
:::
